issues.claim: V06 §6.8 (6) (l. 3763–3767): "A dossier-bound document's epochs are the port's cadence (§4.11 *The clock*) and are never coarsened … each priced at 6.1–6.2 inside §12's waits for a dossier change and an open from SettlementForge." A catch-up folds an epoch at every year end it crosses (§4.11 *The clock* (4): "a catch-up batch follows the same rule"; V08 l. 1778: "every crossing inside the span adds its own epoch"), and a map opened before its turn "catches up at once" (V08 l. 33). By V06 §6.8 (1)'s own rows a catch-up of N years costs ≈ N × 430 ms at CITY (N × 1 120 ms with three islands) and N × 1 310 ms at METROPOLIS (N × 2 090 ms with islands): past ≈ 23 years at CITY (≈ 8 with three islands) and ≈ 7 at METROPOLIS (≈ 4 with islands) its epochs alone exceed the ten seconds item 119 (a) sets for "a dossier change applied" and "open a map from SettlementForge". The claim is unsupported at the limit; V06 §3.21 has no catch-up row and T-V6-24 times none.
issues.required_change: V06 §6.8 (6) reads: "A dossier-bound document's epochs follow the port's cadence (§4.11 *The clock* (4)) while estimate (1) over a catch-up's epochs fits `advance.budgetMs`; above it the catch-up folds one epoch per k crossed year ends, k the smallest whole number whose estimate fits — every dossier event still at its own week (§4.11 *The clock* (2)), a calamity entering the coarse epoch that holds its week, at its week, the population crossings read into the coarse epochs' targets, the last epoch at the dossier's week, every epoch reading the new digest's slices as every catch-up epoch does (J-V8.25) — the cadence reported in `EpochReport.advance` and the port's report; one epoch over the span always fits (6.8 (3)), so no catch-up is refused or shortened (item 101 R2)." V06 §3.21 adds the row "a dossier catch-up of many years | the coarsened catch-up of V06 §6.8 (6) | simpler shape (coarser epochs) | T-V6-24"; T-V6-24 adds a 20-year and a 100-year catch-up at CITY and METROPOLIS, the sky layer off and on, each p95 ≤ 10 000 ms with the dossier's present facts met exactly; a J-V6 row records the choice over keeping the port's cadence. At their homes (hand-offs, not V06's text): §4.11 *The clock* (4)'s catch-up sentence adds "coarsened under item 119's comfort level by V06 §6.8 (6)" (pipeline); V08's catch-up rule and V08 §6's "an absorb with epochs" row cite V06 §6.8 (6).

V06 §3.20.3 (l. 3089) sets the replay's present as "`W_p` the present — the creation week the base gives (`HostContext.week` or 0)", so a history-first generation's epoch weeks follow the host context; V06 §5.2 *Years* (l. 3495) labels a dossier-bound week by "the host's calendar year when `HostContext` gives one" — a host input item 125 retires, and a field `HostContext` does not have (§14's interface, l. 18159: `week`, `realm`, `audience`, `displayNames`, `line`, `customLibrary`).

issues.claim: V06 §4.1 *Preview*: on Accept, "while the document's head is still the preview fork's base, the commit takes the fork's folded state …; otherwise the epochs fold again under the estimate the preview ran with". An edit between the preview and Accept that raises V06 §6.8's estimate is folded at the preview's cadence without re-estimating — e.g. a CITY century with islands previewed at 12½-year steps (8 epochs, ≈ 9.0 s), then 18 hand-placed accesses added (`epoch.handAccessMs` 60 ms each an epoch): 8 × (1 120 + 1 080) ms ≈ 17.6 s — against item 119 (a2) ("the run COARSENS its cadence … until its estimate fits"). T-V6-23 tests only an unchanged head.
issues.required_change: V06 §4.1 reads "… otherwise the epochs fold again at the cadence V06 §6.8's estimate chooses on the current head (V06 §3.3.2), the card's line naming it where it differs from the preview's"; T-V6-23 adds "an Accept after edits that raise the estimate (hand-placed accesses added on the preview's islands) folds at the re-estimated cadence, inside the comfort level".

issues.claim: Base §8.2 (l. 12456–12458): `weather` is `snow` by default only in a cold or severe winter's snow band — "an arid row never snows by default; a viewer's value stands until the viewer changes it"; §8.2's season bar (l. 12892): "on the `arid` row no ice and no default snow". V05 §5.1 (4) draws snow on an island "as on the ground" while the view's `weather` is `snow`, but V05 §3.23's seasonal row says "an arid row draws no ice and no snow on an island" and T-V5-34 (d) "the arid fixture draws no ice and no snow on any island in any week", dropping "by default": under a viewer's `snow` in an arid row the ground draws snow and V05's two statements disagree about the island.
issues.required_change: V05 §3.23's seasonal row reads "… an arid row draws no ice on an island, and no snow while the viewer has set no `weather` (a viewer's `snow` lies on the island as on the ground, §8.2) …"; T-V5-34 (d) reads "the arid fixture, with no viewer `weather`, draws no ice and no snow on any island in any week, and with a viewer's `snow` draws the island's snow exactly where the ground's lies; …".

issues.claim: §12.1 (l. 15649) counts among the comfort level's waits "an open from SettlementForge (with its load verification and any migration, §2.9, §11.3)". §2.9 step 3 runs the verification replay in parallel ("no edit waits for the verification replay"); §12.6's *Replay and load verification* (l. 15954, l. 15958): "a century of history verifies within V06 §6.2's century bound, ≤ 115 s at CITY, off the path to the picture … Verification never delays the picture or an edit"; V06 §6.3 (l. 3667) the same; V12 §3.15.9 (2) times the open "to the complete result — the map's final complete frame". Read literally, §12.1 puts a CITY century document's ≈ 113 s verification inside the open's ten seconds, where every other statement keeps it off the path.
issues.required_change: §12.1's list reads "… an open from SettlementForge (to the editable complete map — the load's digest checks and any migration included; the verification replay runs after it, off the path, §2.9 step 3, §12.6) …".

V06 carries none of it: no text names item 122, a crisis look, a camp's placement or `reconstruction`; `ConditionOverlay` is read only for the Works share (V06 §3.13 (6), l. 2233).
issues.required_change: Write V06's item-122 part at build depth as new design: (1) **the aftermath** (item 122 (a)) — what a crisis leaves reaches the map only through the next epoch: the calamity as an `EpochInputs.events` entry (DR28) run by the hazards phase (V06 §3.11), deaths and exodus through the epoch's `populationTarget`, ruined institutions and a burned quarter through the hazard's ops at the calamity's `targets`, settled newcomers through growth (V06 §3.6) — never a write from a look; (2) **the camp at the growth frontier** — a pure query on the growth phase (where V06 §3.6's spread step would seat a given number of households next, by the same rules and keyed draws, drawing nothing new), read by the refugee camp's placement in §10.2's crisis look table and §8.2's rows, so newcomers who stay become the next epoch's suburb where the camp stood; its fallback (no frontier: the approach road by a gate, item 122 (b)); (3) **reconstruction as Works** — the `reconstruction` archetype's `ConditionOverlay` read by the works phase (V06 §3.13 (6), §4.11 *Works* (10)), the disaster's ruined look giving way to the rebuild's Works scaffolding with no week drawing both; (4) the lifecycle and edges: a look standing when its aftermath epoch folds, a condition with no calamity, the aftermath epoch undone while the look stands, a replay epoch (the look only in the view's week), a standalone map (preview only, no aftermath); a T-V6 clause (the camp inside the next epoch's growth placement for the same households; the model and hash identical with crisis looks on and off; the aftermath equal to the calamity path's result); a J-V6 row; §1b wiring rows (producer and readers); §1.2's hook row; V06 §8's price; the head's item range widened to the highest item V06 cites.

issues.required_change: Write V06's item-123 part at build depth as new design: (1) **the decay level** (0–1) per building lineage at a week — a pure function of its `Existence` state (`abandoned`, `decayed`, `ruined`; `reused` and a repaired building below them), the years since it was abandoned (derived from the week of the epoch whose op last set it `abandoned`, read from its `EpochRecord`, never a stored counter — or a stored field with its §2.12 lifecycle rows) and V11's rate by material (timber faster than stone), monotone non-decreasing while the building stays abandoned, decayed or ruined, so damage only accumulates (item 123 (b)); (2) **restoration** — `reused`, `reoccupy` from derelict and a repair lower the level by a stated rule, the damage leaving in reverse threshold order, a repaired element drawn in patch material (item 114's patchwork); (3) **history** — a building first met ruined in item 113's replay gets its plan as built, then its damage at the level its replayed years give, and time scrubbing (V06 §3.15) reads the level at each frame's week, so one plan is seen aging (item 123 (a)); (4) edges: a building abandoned at generation (no abandonment epoch: the level from its state and V11's default age), a building ruined by a hazard rather than by decay, a successor lineage rebuilt on a trace (a new plan, no damage carried), the restoring epoch undone, negative weeks in the replay; a T-V6 clause (the level monotone in years while abandoned, reversed on restoration, the same at a given seed, week and lineage on every engine; plan ids unchanged); a J-V6 row; a §2.12 lifecycle row and §1b wiring rows (readers: V03's damage layer, V02's exterior, V04's cellars and crypts, the panel); V06 §8's price; the head's item range widened.
